{"commits":[{"authoredDate":"2026-09-17T20:21:18Z","authors":[{"email":"jerimiah797@gmail.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjE1ODQyODI=","login":"jerimiah797","name":"Jerimiah Ham"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-17T20:21:18Z","messageBody":"As a Starlette BaseHTTPMiddleware it replaced the receive channel with
one that never delivered http.disconnect to the endpoint, so
request.is_disconnected() answered False however long ago the caller had
gone -- and since it is installed unconditionally, no handler could
notice a disconnect at all. That is #208, found by #204, which measured
scroll_to_element sweeping a simulator for 413s and 523s on behalf of a
client that left at 180s: holding a device the next caller wanted, and
swiping it while they used it.

The rewrite follows TimelineMiddleware, the pure-ASGI middleware already
here. What it has to get right is mechanical, and each of these is a
place it could have gone quietly wrong:

- ASGI header names are lowercase bytes, not a case-insensitive
  mapping, and values are undecoded. The first occurrence of a repeated
  header wins, as Starlette's Headers.get does.
- The public list is matched against scope["path"], which is what
  request.url.path read.
- The 401 is hand-built as http.response.start + http.response.body,
  with the body JSONResponse produced, byte for byte, including
  content-length.
- lifespan and websocket scopes pass straight through.

Two deliberate differences:

- An empty configured key now authorises nobody. The old code compared
  X-API-Key against it with "" as the default for a missing header, so
  an empty key accepted every request that sent no header. ServerConfig
  always generates one, so this guards a state that should not arise --
  which is what the old code assumed too.
- Keys are compared with hmac.compare_digest rather than ==.

tests/test_auth_middleware.py was written against the old middleware
first, so the rewrite had to reproduce it rather than be described
afterwards: 29 of its 31 tests passed before this change, and the two
that failed are the empty-key guard and the disconnect.

Live: tests/conformance/test_auth.py -- every operation in the schema
against a missing token, a wrong bearer token and a wrong X-API-Key,
plus a valid-key control -- passes identically against a server built
from this branch and one built from main's middleware. 10 passed both.","messageHeadline":"Make APIKeyMiddleware pure ASGI, so handlers can see a disconnect","oid":"43c9b035749c9f99ae06122451955f526dfa3e0b"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-17T20:27:22Z","authors":[{"email":"jerimiah797@gmail.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjE1ODQyODI=","login":"jerimiah797","name":"Jerimiah Ham"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-17T20:27:22Z","messageBody":"Mutation testing the rewrite left two survivors, and one of them is the
kind of mistake this layer exists to prevent:

- Comparing the key with `startswith` rather than an equality accepted
  every prefix of the real key, so `Bearer q` would have been enough.
  Nothing tested a truncated key in either header.
- Which of two repeated headers wins was untested, so taking the last
  rather than the first -- the shape of a smuggling trick, and a
  difference from Starlette's own Headers.get -- passed.

16 mutants of the middleware now, all killed.","messageHeadline":"Pin the header rules the middleware inherited","oid":"13b0249ec6f79376bc6df4efca7a568c21865034"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-17T22:15:38Z","authors":[{"email":"jerimiah797@gmail.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjE1ODQyODI=","login":"jerimiah797","name":"Jerimiah Ham"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-17T22:15:38Z","messageBody":"…nects

dev-34's review of #228 (PR comment 5721896017) found an auth bypass
that this PR introduced, and it is the shape this layer exists to
prevent.

`expected = self.api_key.encode("latin-1", errors="ignore")` dropped
every character that would not encode, so the key compared against was
not the key configured. Reproduced both ways:

- key `abc<emoji>def` accepted the header `abcdef`, and refused the
  real key;
- key `<emoji><emoji>` encoded to nothing, so `Authorization: Bearer `
  with an empty token authorised the request.

~/.quern/api-key is a file a user can edit, and ServerConfig only
generates one when it is missing or empty, so one pasted smart quote
reaches this. The old BaseHTTPMiddleware code failed closed both times.
It is now a UTF-8 encode with an empty-result guard, which also makes a
non-ASCII key work rather than locking its owner out.

The review's other finding was mine to fix too: TimelineMiddleware
replays the buffered request body forever, so for the ten endpoints it
wraps -- `tap_element` among them, the one whose sweep motivated the
guard -- nothing after the body reached the endpoint, disconnects
included. It now delivers the body once and delegates. Measured live
with a timeline recording and the request aborted after 4s: the sweep
stops after 3 swipes, where the review measured it running to the end.

Also pinned, each a mutant that survived: the lossy encode, the empty
expected key, `Bearer` without its separating space, a scope with no
headers, and a method exemption (CORS answers preflights above auth, so
an OPTIONS hole here would be invisible rather than harmless). The
constant-time comparison now says in the code that no test can tell it
from `==`.

23 mutants across both middlewares, all killed. Unit suite 2634.","messageHeadline":"Compare the whole key, and stop the timeline middleware eating discon…","oid":"3e20b24204b6c787f91f3040b5c69223d4c60dfd"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-18T20:27:49Z","authors":[{"email":"jerimiah797@gmail.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjE1ODQyODI=","login":"jerimiah797","name":"Jerimiah Ham"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-18T20:27:49Z","messageBody":"A second review of #228 confirmed the bypass fix holds -- it attacked
the key comparison at the wire level under both of uvicorn's HTTP
parsers, and the tests added with the fix do fail against the bypassed
code -- and found six lesser things. The one that mattered was a
regression traded in for the disconnect fix.

`Request.is_disconnected()` reads the channel inside an already
cancelled scope and discards whatever is not a disconnect. The
timeline middleware's replay returned the buffered body without ever
awaiting, so there was no checkpoint for that cancellation to land on:
the body was handed over, thrown away, and the endpoint's later
`await request.body()` waited on the real channel, which says nothing
until the client leaves. A handler that polled before reading its body
hung until the disconnect it was polling for. It is not reachable
today, because FastAPI parses the Pydantic body before the handler
runs, but #204's guard polls exactly these endpoints. The replay now
yields first.

The rest:

- `~/.quern/api-key` is refused at startup when it holds non-ASCII
  characters, naming the file. No client can send such a key -- httpx
  raises UnicodeEncodeError, node's Headers a TypeError -- so the
  server would start and refuse everything. This also corrects the
  claim that the UTF-8 fix made such keys work: it made them compare
  correctly, which nothing can exercise.
- The key is encoded once, in __init__, so an unencodable key fails at
  startup rather than on an unauthenticated request.
- The trailing-space assertion is re-scoped. Measured on the wire, it
  was three different mechanisms behind one claim: httptools strips a
  leading space but not a trailing one, h11 strips both, a test client
  strips neither. The middleware's own rule -- an exact match -- is
  what this code owns.
- Pinned, each a surviving mutant: a path-less scope reading as public,
  and a present X-API-Key short-circuiting a good bearer token.
- The ASGI signatures take their Starlette types instead of suppressing
  the linter.

29 mutants across the two middlewares and the config loader, all
killed. Unit suite 2641.","messageHeadline":"Keep the buffered body when a handler asks about the disconnect first","oid":"ef7d8d9abaf2c6d62f9383b8d0d49c065ad00fa5"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-18T22:10:51Z","authors":[{"email":"jerimiah797@gmail.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjE1ODQyODI=","login":"jerimiah797","name":"Jerimiah Ham"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-18T22:10:51Z","messageBody":"Live-testing the new guard showed it working and reading badly: the
message that says what to do arrived under a dataclass traceback, and
that sentence is the whole value of the check. Starting with a
non-ASCII key file now prints the reason and exits 1.

The construction moved into `_config_or_exit` so this has a seam a test
can drive; `_cmd_start` reaches it only after port checks and daemon
logic that a test has no business running.

Verified against a server started with QUERN_STATE_DIR pointed at a
scratch directory holding a key with a smart quote in it: the reason,
no traceback, exit 1. An ASCII key in the same directory serves
normally. The real ~/.quern/api-key was not touched.","messageHeadline":"Stop with the reason when the api-key file cannot be used","oid":"209ce2004e3d16ec557c5a444631d87dfb244a76"}]}

What I did: - read #208 and both versions of `server/auth.py`; - exercised the middleware directly over ~30 key and header shapes; - ran a scratch uvicorn on port 9199 with a throwaway key, for the 401 shape, HEAD, OPTIONS, CORS and live disconnects; - ran 9 mutants against a `git archive` copy (tests: 37 passed). **The rewrite is right in its essentials** — path semantics, header parsing, the byte-identical 401, non-http scopes, and the disconnect fix, which I reproduced live. **One finding is an auth bypass and should block merge.** Given this is the only review the PR gets, I'd want a second pair of eyes on whatever fix lands for it. ### High — auth bypass **B-1. `encode("latin-1", errors="ignore")` silently shortens the key, and can empty it.** (Verified, two ways.) `server/auth.py`, `_has_valid_key`: `expected = self.api_key.encode("latin-1", errors="ignore")`. Dropping the characters it can't encode means the key that is checked is not the key that was configured: | configured key | request header | result | |---|---|---| | `abc🔑def` | `X-API-Key: abcdef` | **200** — a shorter key authenticates | | `abc🔑def` | `X-API-Key: abc🔑def` (correct, UTF-8) | 401 — the real key is refused | | `🔑🔑` | `Authorization: Bearer ` (empty token) | **200** — full bypass | The last row is the bad one: with a key that has no latin-1-encodable characters, `expected` is `b""`, and `Bearer ` with nothing after it compares equal. That's a header anyone can send, with no knowledge of anything. Reachable because the key is read from `~/.quern/api-key`, a user-editable file (`server/config.py:52-62`): `ServerConfig` generates a key only when that file is missing or empty, and otherwise uses its stripped contents as-is. Anyone who pastes a key containing a non-ASCII character — a smart quote, an emoji, a Cyrillic letter, a mangled copy-paste — gets this. The old code failed *closed* in both cases: it compared `str` to `str`, so a non-ASCII key refused everyone, including the legitimate client. This is the same class as the empty-key case the PR already guards, one step along: "the configured key is not what gets compared". Suggested fix — encode as UTF-8, which is what a client actually puts on the wire, and refuse an empty result: ```python expected = self.api_key.encode("utf-8") if not expected: return False ``` That also makes a non-ASCII key *work* rather than lock its owner out. Rejecting a non-ASCII key at config load would be a reasonable belt-and-braces addition. Either way, a test with a non-ASCII configured key belongs in the suite — mutant A3 (`errors="ignore"` → strict) survives today, which is how this stayed invisible. ### Medium — the disconnect claim is not quite "every endpoint" **B-2. `TimelineMiddleware` re-breaks disconnects for its action endpoints while a timeline is active.** (Verified live.) `server/screenshot_timeline.py:175`: when a timeline is active and the path is in `ACTION_FORMATTERS`, the request body is buffered and `receive` is replaced by ```python async def cached_receive(): return {"type": "http.request", "body": body_bytes} ``` which answers `http.request` forever and never delivers `http.disconnect` — the same shape of bug as `BaseHTTPMiddleware`. On a scratch stack of CORS → auth → timeline, with a timeline active and the client aborting after 1s: - `/api/v1/device/ui/scroll-to-element` (not an action path): disconnect seen after 0.75s; - `/api/v1/device/ui/tap-element` (an action path): **ran to completion, disconnect never seen**. `tap-element` is the endpoint #204 added its guard for, so the gap lands on the case that motivated all of this — but only while a screenshot timeline is recording. Not a defect in this PR, and I wouldn't hold the merge for it: the fix is to yield the buffered body once and then delegate to the real `receive`. Worth a follow-up issue, and worth qualifying "fixes disconnect detection for every endpoint at once" in #208 and the CHANGELOG. ### Low — test gaps (each verified by a surviving mutant) - **A9:** adding an OPTIONS exemption to the path check (`if scope.get("method") == "OPTIONS" or ...`) survives every test. In production CORS answers preflights above auth, so it is latent — but a blanket method exemption is exactly the change that should fail loudly. A test for OPTIONS to a protected path with no key → 401 would pin it. - **A4:** `startswith(b"Bearer ")` → `startswith(b"Bearer")` survives. Not exploitable as far as I can tell, but `Authorization: Bearerabc` is untested. - **A5:** `scope.get("headers") or ()` → `scope["headers"]` survives; the defensive `.get` is untested. - **A2:** `hmac.compare_digest` → `==` survives, and can't be caught by a behavioural test. Worth a line of comment in the code so a later refactor doesn't quietly drop the constant-time compare. ### Loose ends - #208's landing checklist says to restore the 499 to `docs/api-reference.md` and the `scroll_to_element` MCP description. Neither mentions 499 on this branch. - I couldn't find `tests/conformance/test_auth.py` anywhere in the tree, so the "122 operations, before and after" gate can't be run from this branch. If it lives elsewhere, it's worth running before merge, and worth a pointer from the issue. ### Verified correct (no action) - **Paths:** on Starlette 1.6, `URL(scope=scope).path` is `scope["path"]` with no `root_path` prefix, so swapping `request.url.path` for `scope["path"]` changes nothing, including under a mount. `PUBLIC_PATHS` matches main's tuple exactly, item for item. - **Path shapes, all 401 (unchanged from main):** `/health/`, `//health`, `/HEALTH`, `/docs/oauth2-redirect`, `/health/secrets`, and a scope with no `path` key at all. Public paths still 200. Percent-encoding can't help an attacker here: uvicorn decodes before the scope, and a decoded path has to *equal* a public entry, which only public routes do. - **Headers:** first occurrence wins for both headers, matching `Headers.get`; a good `X-API-Key` still wins after a bad `Authorization`; scheme matching stays case-sensitive; `compare_digest` on different-length bytes returns False without raising. - **The 401:** byte-identical to what `JSONResponse` sent (same `separators`, `content-type: application/json`, `content-length: 39`), single body message, no `more_body`. Live: CORS headers are still applied to it, a preflight with `Origin` + `Access-Control-Request-Method` is answered by CORS above auth, `HEAD` gets 401 with no body, and keep-alive survives a 401 whose request body was never read (POST 401 then GET 200 on one connection). - **The disconnect fix itself:** confirmed live through CORS → auth on a scratch server (disconnect seen 0.75s after a 1s abort). The reasoning generalises: the middleware now passes `receive` through untouched, so anything that respects it works, subject to B-2. - **Deliberate changes:** the empty-key guard is right, and `compare_digest` is the correct call. Second review (independent reviewer, in its own worktree) The bypass fix was reviewed adversarially by a second agent, since the first version of this code introduced a hole its own tests missed. **Verdict: the fix holds, and would not block merge.** It attacked `_has_valid_key` at the wire level against a real uvicorn with a throwaway key `thr0waway-🔑-key` on ports 9251/9252, under **both** HTTP parsers: | request | httptools | h11 | |---|---|---| | exact UTF-8 key, either header | 200 | 200 | | the old latin-1-lossy form of the key | 401 | 401 | | empty bearer token | 401 | 401 | | obs-folded key | 400 | 401 | | repeated header, wrong first | 401 | 401 | It also confirmed the new tests **fail against the bypassed code** (reverting the encode is killed by 2 tests; removing the empty guard by 1), and that `_status` is a real 401 oracle rather than a recorder. ### Acted on - **F1 (medium, the one real regression):** `is_disconnected()` reads the channel in an already-cancelled scope and discards non-disconnect messages. My replay returned the buffered body with no `await`, so the cancellation had nowhere to land: the body was consumed and discarded, and the endpoint's later `body()` waited on the real channel until the client left. A handler polling before reading its body hung until the disconnect it was polling for. The replay now yields first. Two tests, and removing the checkpoint kills one. - **F2:** my "a non-ASCII key now works" claim was wrong — httpx and node both refuse to send one, so it was a silent lockout rather than a capability. `~/.quern/api-key` with non-ASCII content is now refused at startup, naming the file. Changelog corrected. - **F6:** the key is encoded once in `__init__`, so an unencodable key fails at startup rather than per request. - **F3:** the trailing-space assertion is re-scoped to the middleware's own rule. On the wire it was three mechanisms behind one claim (httptools strips leading not trailing, h11 strips both, TestClient strips neither). - **F4, F5:** both surviving mutants are pinned — a path-less scope reading as public, and a present `X-API-Key` short-circuiting a good bearer token. - **Minor:** the ASGI signatures now carry their Starlette types instead of `# noqa: ANN001`. 29 mutants across the two middlewares and the config loader, all killed. Unit suite:
